open_points.subject: Registry validation fields used by project and access-management guards
open_points.text: A5 says grant and assignment operations trust `is_active`, the project guard trusts `status`, and A6 says the gateway does not check that `exists`, `is_active` and `status` agree; R0-24 nevertheless says no new grant or assignment is created for an archived project.
open_points.question: When a decoded validation answer has `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, and `is_active=true`, must creation of a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant succeed or be rejected as an archived project?
options: Trust `is_active` for access-management creation and allow it
Treat `status="archived"` as authoritative and reject it
Reject inconsistent Registry answers as a boundary/schema failure
open_points.default_guess: Reject the inconsistent answer as `schema_mismatch` and create nothing.

witness.initial: An active administrator is authorized for access management; no grant exists for project P; Registry regards P as archived, and its validation response is decoded as `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, `is_active=true`.
events: The administrator requests creation of a viewer grant for P.
The portal validates P through Registry.
outcomes: Following the changed A5/A6 caller rule, grant creation trusts `is_active=true` and succeeds.
Following R0-24 and the registry-status policy, creation is rejected because P is archived.
witness.observer: The administrator and the persisted grant repository see whether the grant was created.

open_points.subject: Snapshot import when Registry validation fails operationally
open_points.text: A4 says an unanswered Registry validation fails the operation through A6, while A7 says an authenticated import authorization failure is recorded as only `unknown_project`, `scope_denied`, or `archived_project`; `ImportRejectReason` has no timeout, transport, HTTP, schema, or identity-mismatch reason.
open_points.question: What response, import-record behavior, outcome, and reason apply when Registry validation raises `timeout`, `transport_error`, `http_error`, `schema_mismatch`, or `identity_mismatch` during an authenticated snapshot import?
options: Propagate the Registry boundary failure and write no import record
Record a rejected import as `unknown_project`
Add or otherwise define a distinct Registry-unavailable rejection
open_points.default_guess: Propagate the Registry boundary failure and write no import or audit record, because no permitted `ImportRejectReason` represents it.

witness.initial: An active estimate producer has a valid bearer credential, import capability, and an active grant for project P; the publication body is valid.
events: Registry validation for P times out.
outcomes: The timeout escapes as a boundary/server failure and no `SnapshotImportRecord` is written.
The failure is concealed as `unknown_project`, producing a fresh rejected import record and audit record.
witness.observer: The producer sees whether an `import_id` is returned and can later attempt to read that result.

open_points.subject: Expense-intake validation versus the common authorization guard
open_points.text: A4 requires every project-scoped operation to check project access before capability and Registry lifecycle, but A7 orders expense creation as recognition status, contract version, capability, active project, allocation validation, then replay.
open_points.question: Does expense creation validate recognition content before invoking the complete A4 guard, or must project access be checked before contract-version and other content checks?
options: Run the complete A4 guard before recognition/content validation
Validate recognition status and contract version before the A4 guard
Treat A7's `capability, active project` step as the whole A4 guard but retain its position after contract validation
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate first, then run the complete A4 guard, then validate recognition content.

witness.initial: An active operator has a valid session and expense capability but no assignment for project P; the submitted recognition has an unsupported contract version.
events: The operator submits expense creation for P.
outcomes: A4 checks project access first and refuses because the assignment is absent, without classifying the contract version.
A7 rejects the unsupported contract version before checking project access.
witness.observer: A focused use-case test or instrumented assignment repository sees whether the project-scope lookup occurred and which rejection was raised.

open_points.subject: HTTP request-body size bound
open_points.text: A25 requires request bodies to be bounded by runtime settings, but A30 specifies `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` and does not give a request-body limit key, type, requiredness, default, or numeric value.
open_points.question: Which runtime setting defines the request-body ceiling, and what are its environment name, validation rule, requiredness, and environment defaults?
options: Introduce a required request-body byte-limit setting
Use a fixed source constant
Apply the binary-read limit to request bodies as well
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate required positive-integer `request_body_max_bytes` setting.

witness.initial: A deployment supplies every environment variable and value explicitly listed in A30, but no unlisted request-body setting.
events: A caller sends a JSON request body of 2 MiB.
outcomes: An implementation with a 1 MiB assumed ceiling rejects it before the handler.
An implementation with a 10 MiB assumed ceiling admits it.
witness.observer: The caller sees rejection versus handler execution.

open_points.subject: Viewer-entry sliding-window boundary
open_points.text: A25 says attempts already `within the last ... seconds` count, but also says entries `older than the window` are dropped; it does not state whether an entry exactly at `now - window` is retained or dropped.
open_points.question: At the exact window boundary, is an earlier admitted viewer-entry attempt still counted?
options: Use a half-open window and drop timestamps `<= now - window`
Use a closed window and drop only timestamps `< now - window`
open_points.default_guess: Drop entries at or before `now - window`, using `(now - window, now]`.

witness.initial: The limit is one attempt per 60 seconds, and an attempt from address A was admitted at exactly 12:00:00.
events: At exactly 12:01:00, A makes another viewer-entry attempt.
outcomes: The first entry is outside the half-open window, so the new attempt is admitted and counted.
The first entry is retained at the closed boundary, so the new attempt receives HTTP 429.
witness.observer: The viewer sees admission versus HTTP 429.

open_points.subject: Viewer-entry limiter memory bound
open_points.text: A25 calls the viewer-entry limiter bounded-memory, then states that there is no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction, so arbitrarily many client-address keys can remain during one window.
open_points.question: Must the limiter impose a global memory/key bound with defined eviction or refusal behavior, or is memory intentionally unbounded across distinct client addresses within a window?
options: Keep the stated no-cap algorithm and remove the bounded-memory guarantee
Define a global key/entry cap and deterministic eviction
Define a global cap that refuses new keys instead of evicting
open_points.default_guess: Define a global cap with deterministic eviction that preserves existing rate-limit decisions as far as possible.

witness.initial: Address A has already used all allowed attempts in the current window.
events: Arbitrarily many distinct addresses each make one admitted attempt before the window expires.
Address A retries before its original entries expire.
outcomes: Following `no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction`, all keys remain and A receives HTTP 429, while memory can grow without bound.
Following the bounded-memory requirement, some entry or key must be evicted or refused; if A's key is evicted, its retry is admitted.
witness.observer: The service operator sees memory growth, and address A may see admission versus HTTP 429.

open_points.subject: Response `X-Request-Id` generation and trust
open_points.text: A25 requires every response to carry `an X-Request-Id` but gives no source, syntax, uniqueness, maximum length, handling of an inbound header, or relation to logging.
open_points.question: Must the service always generate the request ID, may it accept or echo a caller-supplied value, and what validation and logging rules apply?
options: Always generate a fresh server-owned identifier and ignore inbound values
Validate and reuse a caller-supplied identifier, otherwise generate one
Echo any caller-supplied value
open_points.default_guess: Always generate a fresh server-owned UUID and use the same value in response and request-correlated logs.

witness.initial: A caller can send arbitrary request headers.
events: The caller sends `X-Request-Id` containing a chosen long value with a newline-like control character.
outcomes: An implementation echoes or logs the supplied value as the response request ID.
An implementation ignores it and returns a newly generated safe identifier.
witness.observer: The caller sees the returned identifier, and the service operator sees different log-correlation and injection behavior.

open_points.subject: Dependency vulnerability-check command and audited package set
open_points.text: A32 first defines the reproducible check as `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt`, which resolves requirements, and later says the check runs against the built image as `pip-audit --local`, which audits the installed environment.
open_points.question: Are both checks required, or which command and package set is authoritative for deciding whether the deploy passes?
options: Require both the requirements-resolution audit and the installed-image audit
Use only `pip-audit --local` in the built image
Use only `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt`
open_points.default_guess: Require the installed-image `pip-audit --local` result as authoritative, with the requirements audit optional and non-authoritative.

witness.initial: The built image contains transitive package version T1, while a fresh resolution of the four direct pins selects newer transitive version T2; an advisory affects exactly one of T1 and T2.
outcomes: `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt` audits T2 and produces one pass/block decision.
`pip-audit --local` audits shipped T1 and produces the opposite decision.
witness.observer: The deployment pipeline sees whether the release is allowed or blocked.
